messages.content: You are a senior local-inference architect. Answer directly and do not think out loud. Be concise, skeptical, and specific. Return sections named Verdict, Main Risks, Better Design, and Validation.

We have DevRail Router exposing a fast local-coder alias backed by LM Studio Qwen3.6 with concurrency 2, plus a slower local-coder-deep alias backed by llama.cpp Qwen3.8 on CPU/mmap. We want opencode clients to keep requesting local-coder while the router automatically sends high-importance requests to the deep backend. The naive policy is keyword matching on messages containing review, architecture, plan, security, migration, or failing tests. Evaluate this plan and propose a safer first implementation.
You are a pragmatic infrastructure incident reviewer. Answer directly and do not think out loud. Focus on root causes, order of operations, and what to automate next. Keep the answer under 350 words.

During an llm-srv deploy, these events happened: full upstream llama.cpp clone hung until canceled; shallow clone fixed that; CMake then failed because Arch lacked SPIRV-Headers; after adding spirv-headers, llama.cpp built and 77 GB of GGUF shards downloaded; first Qwen3.8 smoke crashed because --n-gpu-layers 999 caused Vulkan out-of-device-memory while LM Studio also used V620 VRAM; CPU/mmap-first with 32k context worked; a later deploy got slow because get_url rechecked huge existing shards until stat-before-download was added. What are the real lessons and the next two automation changes?
